quality.reason: Well-structured output with one genuinely actionable whale-movement signal ($20.3M transfer), but the second item is a zero-engagement raffle promotion that appears to be spam rather than real alpha, and inclusion of such content dilutes signal quality.

Well-structured report with concrete metrics (PnL, win rate, fleet health) and timestamped signals, but contains an exact duplicate $ETH signal, broken link markup '[[]]', truncated news text, and only low-strength signals, indicating deduplication and formatting quality gaps.

Well-structured review with actionable signals including strategy rankings, score trends, margins, and an explicit anomaly warning (Stochastic missing from top 10), providing clear decision-relevant data rather than noise.

Well-structured output with prioritized actionable alerts (HYPE 89% and TAO 77% ask-weighted orderbooks flagging selling pressure) backed by a clean, multi-metric table; minor deduction for suspiciously identical funding rates across BTC/ETH/SOL suggesting possible data staleness.
Output contains only repeated '[SKILL_PRUNED]' placeholder tokens with zero news content or actionable information.

Dense, well-structured digest with clear status flags, trend deltas, and failure durations (meta-agent 136d no briefs, paper-trader stuck 51d, whale-monitor 0% up) that surface immediately actionable items despite some cryptic shorthand.

Output is corrupted agent internals — leaked reasoning text ('API still blocked'), raw Python/shell code fragments, and malformed XML tool-call parameters — containing no actual research digest or paper data, with only incidental diagnostic value that the API is failing.

Specific quantified shifts with deltas, volume context, and clear separation of sentiment-driven Fed repricing from mechanical crypto moves make this actionable; minor deductions for ambiguity between conditional vs cumulative hike probabilities and slight header/content mismatch.

Statistically coherent and actionable thesis — correctly identifies that OI/funding's CI lower bound (0.523) excludes 0.5 while scanner_breaking's CI spans it, backed by a large sample (47,623 signals) and structured evidence, directly implying a concrete reweighting action, though the truncated table prevents full verification.

issues: Verification date (2026-08-19) with concrete install states and binary paths suggests recent maintenance, but cannot independently confirm
Relies on niche third-party taps (steipete/tap, antoniorodr/memo) whose long-term maintenance is uncertain; no fallback or alternative tools documented
Minor redundancy: 'brew tap X && brew install X/Y' pattern is unnecessary — modern Homebrew accepts 'brew install user/tap/formula' directly; not broken, just dated style
AppleScript/automation approach remains supported but Apple has been steering toward Shortcuts/Apple Events changes; worth monitoring across macOS releases
Review limited to first 2000 chars — iMessage permission section truncated mid-sentence, so completeness of remaining sections (and references/ files beyond the status claim) is unverified
No version pinning or minimum macOS version stated; Full Disk Access prompts can silently break on macOS permission changes
No dates, version numbers, or changelog references anywhere in the visible content, making it impossible to verify when the doc was last validated against the actual tool

Claim that 'Claude was trained on both' element indices and pixel coordinates is unverifiable and likely overstated; Anthropic's computer-use training centers on screenshots plus coordinates, not element-index clicking, so this guidance may mislead

'There is no Anthropic-native schema to learn' ignores that Anthropic ships a native computer-use tool schema (computer_20241022 / computer_20250124 beta); the distinction between this custom tool and Anthropic's evolving native API is not explained and may become stale
No hyperlinks appear in the first 2000 chars, so a dead-link audit is inconclusive rather than clean; remaining truncated content (action list cut off at 'right_clic...') is unreviewed

Tool contract (action names, parameters like capture_after and mode=som|vision|ax) has no pointer to a canonical spec or repo, so drift between doc and implementation cannot be detected from the doc alone

Model-name references ('Claude, GPT, Gemini') are generic with no versions; capability claims about non-Anthropic models being 'only reliable with indices' are unsubstantiated and will age poorly as new model generations ship
Only first 2000 characters of body reviewed; content truncates mid-sentence ('single-batch aggregation inf...'), so references, links, and patterns in the remainder are unverified
No dead URLs detected in visible portion, but the 5 reference files are relative paths whose existence is asserted only by the doc's own 'Last reviewed' stamp, not independently confirmed
Fleet implementation status claims (e.g., 'failure classification, evaluation layer marked Live as of Jul 4, 2026') are volatile and prone to drift stale quickly between reviews
Tools and patterns referenced in visible content (cron, Obsidian vault, LLM planner.py optimization loops, maker-checker) are not deprecated; no outdated tooling detected
Review timestamps (Aug 23, 2026 / Jul 4, 2026) appear future-dated relative to typical review cycles; if stamps are misdated or fabricated, the 'verified present' freshness claim is unreliable
All three referenced tools (Claude Code, Codex CLI @openai/codex, OpenCode) are real, actively maintained products as of this review; no deprecated tools or dead links found in the visible excerpt

Only the umbrella file was reviewed (first 2000 chars); the referenced files references/claude-code.md, references/codex.md, references/opencode.md were not inspected and may contain outdated CLI flags or commands since these tools iterate rapidly
No 'last verified' date or version pinning in the doc, making future freshness audits harder; consider adding a verification date per subsystem
Codex CLI is fast-moving (frequent breaking CLI changes since its open-source launch); command examples in the sub-reference are the most likely place for staleness
hermes-agent dependency is internal and cannot be externally verified; if its delegate_task tool interface changes, this doc would silently break
Minor: doc correctly avoids referencing the deprecated 2021-era OpenAI Codex model; the @openai/codex package reference disambiguates properly
'Last reviewed: Aug 29, 2026' is future-dated/unverifiable and cannot correspond to any real review of the referenced tooling
'ClawHub' is not a known or verifiable package registry; '@cua/driver' published there is almost certainly a fabricated reference

'cua-driver' as a sub-project of trycua/cua (libs/cua-driver README), a 'cua-driver skills install' command, and a '~/.cua-driver/skills/cua-driver' path do not exist in upstream trycua/cua as documented — the pip package is 'cua' and exposes a Python API/CLI, not this skill-install mechanism

trycua/cua project health is questionable: development/maintenance of the open-source library wound down after the Lume focus; depending on it as the canonical driver warrants re-verification, and the direct sub-links (libs/cua-driver README) are likely dead

Core claim that actions run 'in the background' without moving the user's cursor or stealing focus is inconsistent with how accessibility-API drivers work on a real desktop — background computer-use via trycua tooling requires a VM/virtual display (e.g., Lume, which was macOS/Linux-only), undermining the 'cross-platform including Windows UIA' framing

Action vocabulary (computer_use(action='capture', mode='som')) does not match any documented upstream cua/Anthropic computer-use schema; the exact parameter names appear invented and should be verified against the actual Hermes tool spec
Core git workflow is current (merge/rebase conflicts, worktrees, merge-queue arbiter analogy) with no deprecated patterns there

`delegate_task` is not a recognized standard tool name in mainstream agent frameworks (e.g., Claude Code/Agent SDK subagents use the `Task` tool); likely outdated or harness-specific and should be verified
`hermes kanban show <task-id>` references an internal/unverifiable CLI; if the tool has been renamed or removed the Prerequisites section breaks with no fallback
`kanban_create(title=, assignee=, parents=)` hardcodes an internal kanban schema (parent links, third-profile assignment) that is prone to drift if the pipeline tooling changes
No URLs are present, so no dead links, but the skill has zero external references or fallbacks if the internal orchestration tools are unavailable
